title: Nigerian Peoples & Culture
source_note: Standard Nigerian university 200L GST curriculum on Nigerian peoples and culture: pre-colonial societies and political systems of major ethnic groups, colonialism and amalgamation, independence and nationhood, culture and its elements, traditional institutions, federalism, and national unity/integration issues. Only well-established, widely documented Nigerian facts are used.

questions.question: Culture is best defined as:
options: The totality of a people's way of life, including beliefs, customs, and values
Only the traditional music of a people
A country's system of government alone
The physical geography of a region
questions.correct_answer: The totality of a people's way of life, including beliefs, customs, and values
questions.explanation: Culture encompasses the complete pattern of human knowledge, belief, behaviour, customs, and values shared by a group of people.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a major element of culture?
questions.explanation: Language is a core element of culture, as it carries and transmits a people's knowledge, values, and worldview.

questions.question: Nigeria's three largest ethnic groups are commonly identified as:
questions.explanation: The Hausa-Fulani, Yoruba, and Igbo are widely recognized as Nigeria's three largest and most populous ethnic groups.

questions.question: The pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani political system was predominantly organized around:
options: Independent city-state republics with no chiefs
questions.explanation: Following the Sokoto Jihad led by Usman dan Fodio in the early 19th century, Hausa-Fulani society was organized into emirates headed by emirs under the Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.question: Which pre-colonial Nigerian political system is generally described as lacking centralized kingship and instead relying on councils of elders and age-grades?
questions.explanation: Many traditional Igbo communities were organized as segmentary, largely republican societies governed by councils of elders, age-grades, and title societies rather than centralized kings.

questions.question: The traditional Yoruba political system was typically centred around:
options: Obas (kings) ruling over kingdoms with chiefs and councils
questions.correct_answer: Obas (kings) ruling over kingdoms with chiefs and councils
questions.explanation: Pre-colonial Yoruba society was organized into kingdoms, each ruled by an Oba assisted by chiefs and advisory councils such as the Oyo Mesi in Oyo.

questions.question: The historic Oyo Empire was primarily associated with which Nigerian ethnic group?
questions.explanation: The Oyo Empire was one of the most powerful pre-colonial Yoruba states in what is now south-western Nigeria.

questions.question: The Benin Kingdom, famous for its bronze artworks, was historically ruled by a monarch known as the:
questions.explanation: The Benin Kingdom, located in present-day Edo State, was ruled by a monarch bearing the title Oba, distinct from the Alaafin of Oyo.

questions.question: Britain formally amalgamated the Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria in the year:
questions.explanation: Lord Frederick Lugard amalgamated the Northern and Southern Protectorates into a single entity called Nigeria in 1914.

questions.question: The British colonial administrator most associated with the 1914 amalgamation of Nigeria was:
questions.explanation: Lord Frederick Lugard served as the colonial governor-general who oversaw the amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates in 1914.

questions.question: The colonial administrative strategy in which local traditional rulers were used to govern on behalf of the colonial authority is known as:
questions.explanation: Indirect rule, associated with Lord Lugard, governed colonies through existing traditional rulers and institutions under overall British supervision.

questions.question: Nigeria gained independence from British colonial rule in the year:
questions.explanation: Nigeria became an independent nation on 1 October 1960.

questions.question: Nigeria became a republic, with a Nigerian head of state replacing the British monarch as head of state, in the year:
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a republic on 1 October 1963, when Nnamdi Azikiwe became the country's first President, replacing the British monarch as head of state.

questions.question: Nigeria's first indigenous Prime Minister at independence in 1960 was:
questions.explanation: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa served as Nigeria's first Prime Minister when the country gained independence in 1960.

questions.question: Nigeria's first President (a ceremonial head of state under the 1963 republican constitution) was:
questions.explanation: Nnamdi Azikiwe became Nigeria's first President in 1963 when the country adopted a republican constitution.

questions.question: The Nigerian Civil War (Biafran War) was fought primarily between the Federal Government of Nigeria and the secessionist state of:
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Civil War (1967-1970) was fought between the federal government and the breakaway Eastern Region, which declared itself the Republic of Biafra.

questions.question: The Nigerian Civil War lasted from 1967 to:
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Civil War began in July 1967 and ended in January 1970 with the surrender of Biafran forces.

questions.question: Nigeria currently operates as a federation made up of 36 states and:
questions.explanation: Nigeria is a federation of 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, which serves as the seat of the federal government.

questions.question: Nigeria's federal capital was officially moved from Lagos to Abuja in the year:
questions.explanation: The federal capital of Nigeria was formally relocated from Lagos to Abuja in December 1991.

questions.question: A political system in which power is constitutionally divided between a central government and constituent states is called:
questions.explanation: Federalism is a system of government in which power is shared constitutionally between a central authority and regional/state governments, as practised in Nigeria.

questions.question: The principle in the Nigerian Constitution requiring appointments and resources to reflect the country's diversity and prevent domination by any one group is called:
questions.explanation: The federal character principle is a constitutional provision aimed at ensuring fair representation of Nigeria's diverse ethnic and state groups in government appointments and resources.

questions.question: The traditional Yoruba system of kinship and marriage is generally described as:
options: Patrilineal, tracing descent through the father's line
Purely matriarchal with no male authority
questions.correct_answer: Patrilineal, tracing descent through the father's line
questions.explanation: Traditional Yoruba society, like most major Nigerian ethnic groups, is patrilineal, tracing lineage and inheritance primarily through the father's line.

questions.question: In many traditional Nigerian societies, the practice of a man paying a bride price to the family of his bride before marriage is called:
questions.explanation: Bride price is a traditional practice in many Nigerian cultures in which the groom or his family gives money or gifts to the bride's family as part of the marriage process.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'extended family' as practised traditionally in Nigerian societies?
options: A family unit that includes parents, children, and other relatives such as grandparents, uncles, and cousins
A family limited strictly to parents and their children
A family made up only of unrelated individuals
A family structure found only in urban areas
questions.correct_answer: A family unit that includes parents, children, and other relatives such as grandparents, uncles, and cousins
questions.explanation: The extended family system, common across traditional Nigerian societies, includes a wider network of relatives beyond the nuclear family.

questions.question: Nigeria's national motto is:
options: Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress
questions.correct_answer: Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress
questions.explanation: Nigeria's official national motto is 'Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress'.

questions.question: The colours of the Nigerian national flag are:
questions.explanation: The Nigerian flag consists of three vertical bands: green, white, and green, symbolizing agriculture/natural wealth (green) and peace/unity (white).

questions.question: Nigeria's currency is called the:
questions.explanation: The naira is the official currency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of Nigeria's major traditional religions practised before the widespread arrival of Christianity and Islam?
questions.explanation: Before the spread of Christianity and Islam, various indigenous African traditional religions, with beliefs in a supreme being, deities, and ancestral spirits, were practised across Nigeria.

questions.question: Islam was introduced into what is now northern Nigeria significantly earlier than into much of the south, spreading mainly through:
questions.explanation: Islam spread into what is now northern Nigeria over centuries mainly through trans-Saharan trade routes and the activities of Islamic scholars and clerics, well before European colonization.

questions.question: Christianity in Nigeria spread significantly through the activities of:
options: European and returnee missionaries from the 19th century onward
questions.correct_answer: European and returnee missionaries from the 19th century onward
questions.explanation: Christian missionary activity, including by European missionaries and freed slaves who returned to West Africa, was central to the spread of Christianity in Nigeria from the 19th century.

questions.question: The process by which one culture adopts or is influenced by contact with another culture is called:
questions.explanation: Acculturation refers to the process of cultural change and exchange that results from prolonged contact between different cultures.

questions.question: Which of these is a common cause of culture change in contemporary Nigerian society?
options: Complete rejection of all foreign contact
questions.explanation: Western-style education, urbanization, and modern technology are widely recognized as major drivers of cultural change in contemporary Nigerian society.

questions.question: 'National integration' in the Nigerian context primarily refers to:
options: The process of unifying Nigeria's diverse ethnic and religious groups into a cohesive nation
The merging of Nigeria with neighbouring countries
The division of Nigeria into smaller independent states
questions.correct_answer: The process of unifying Nigeria's diverse ethnic and religious groups into a cohesive nation
questions.explanation: National integration refers to efforts to build unity and a shared sense of nationhood among Nigeria's many ethnic, religious, and cultural groups.

questions.question: Which of the following is commonly cited as a major challenge to national unity in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Ethnic and religious diversity, when poorly managed, has historically been identified as a major source of tension challenging national unity in Nigeria.

questions.question: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) scheme was established in Nigeria mainly to:
options: Promote national unity and integration among youth from different regions
Recruit soldiers for the military only
questions.correct_answer: Promote national unity and integration among youth from different regions
questions.explanation: The NYSC scheme, established in 1973, was created partly in response to the civil war to foster national unity by posting graduates to serve in states other than their own.

questions.question: Traditional rulers in contemporary Nigeria (such as Obas, Emirs, and Obis) generally function primarily as:
options: Custodians of culture and tradition with mostly advisory/ceremonial roles
The supreme constitutional heads of the federal government
Elected members of the National Assembly
Judges of the Federal High Court
questions.correct_answer: Custodians of culture and tradition with mostly advisory/ceremonial roles
questions.explanation: Under Nigeria's current constitutional framework, traditional rulers hold no formal executive powers but serve as respected custodians of culture with advisory and ceremonial influence.

questions.question: The title used for a traditional ruler among the Igbo in many communities is:
questions.explanation: 'Igwe' is a common traditional title for a paramount ruler in many Igbo communities, though titles can vary by locality.

questions.question: The Sultan of Sokoto is traditionally regarded as the spiritual leader of which major Nigerian religious community?
options: Traditional worshippers in the Niger Delta
questions.explanation: The Sultan of Sokoto holds a position of great religious significance and is widely regarded as a leading spiritual authority for Muslims in Nigeria.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'cultural relativism'?
options: The view that a culture's practices should be understood within its own context rather than judged by another culture's standards
The belief that one culture is universally superior to all others
The rejection of all cultural practices as invalid
A legal doctrine specific to Nigerian courts
questions.correct_answer: The view that a culture's practices should be understood within its own context rather than judged by another culture's standards
questions.explanation: Cultural relativism holds that cultural practices and beliefs should be evaluated within their own cultural context rather than judged against the standards of another culture.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of material culture?
questions.explanation: Material culture refers to physical, tangible objects created and used by a society, such as clothing, tools, and artefacts, as opposed to non-material culture like beliefs and values.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of non-material culture?
options: A society's belief system and values
questions.correct_answer: A society's belief system and values
questions.explanation: Non-material culture consists of intangible aspects of a society, such as beliefs, values, norms, and language, as distinguished from physical objects (material culture).

questions.question: Nigeria has how many officially recognized states as of the country's current federal structure?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is currently composed of 36 states, in addition to the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja.

questions.question: Which of these is one of Nigeria's three former regions before the creation of additional states began in 1963/1967?
questions.explanation: At independence in 1960, Nigeria was divided into three regions: Northern, Western, and Eastern, before later state creation exercises expanded this number.

questions.question: A key value commonly emphasized across many traditional Nigerian societies regarding respect for elders is:
options: Deference and honour shown to older members of the community
Preference for the opinions of children over adults
Isolation of elders from community decisions
questions.correct_answer: Deference and honour shown to older members of the community
questions.explanation: Respect for elders is a widely shared traditional value across many Nigerian ethnic groups, reflecting the importance placed on age and experience.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'ethnicity'?
options: A shared identity based on common ancestry, culture, language, or traditions
A person's individual political party affiliation
A classification based solely on physical geography
A term used only for religious groups
questions.correct_answer: A shared identity based on common ancestry, culture, language, or traditions
questions.explanation: Ethnicity refers to group identity rooted in shared ancestry, culture, language, and traditions distinguishing one group from another.

questions.question: Nigeria is often described as a multi-ethnic and multi-lingual nation with how many or more distinct languages spoken across the country, according to widely cited linguistic surveys?
questions.explanation: Linguistic surveys widely document Nigeria as one of the most linguistically diverse countries in the world, with several hundred distinct indigenous languages spoken.

questions.question: English serves as Nigeria's official language mainly because of:
options: The legacy of British colonial rule
It being the most widely spoken indigenous language
Its adoption by the African Union
questions.correct_answer: The legacy of British colonial rule
questions.explanation: English became Nigeria's official language as a direct legacy of British colonial administration, and it continues to serve as a unifying language of government, education, and commerce.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why the study of Nigerian Peoples and Culture is included in Nigerian university general studies programmes?
options: To foster national consciousness, unity, and appreciation of Nigeria's cultural diversity among students
To train students exclusively as professional historians
To replace the need for any other general education course
To prepare students only for careers in tourism
questions.correct_answer: To foster national consciousness, unity, and appreciation of Nigeria's cultural diversity among students
questions.explanation: This GST course is designed to build students' awareness, understanding, and appreciation of Nigeria's diverse peoples and cultures, promoting national consciousness and unity.
